name: StockBear v0.1.0-dev5
body:
# StockBear v0.1.0-dev5 — development prerelease

StockBear is an independent C++17 UCI chess engine. Board, legal move
generation, state management, alpha-beta search, evaluation, dead-position
analysis and the UCI controller are implemented in this repository; it
neither embeds nor calls another engine to select moves. This is an early
development release, not a stable or leading-strength engine.

## What this release is, and what it is not

dev5 is the first release with a **measured, pre-registered strength gain over
the previous release binary**. The gain comes from a tuned evaluation
parameter set plus one search option, both delivered as UCI options — the
default configuration of the binary is unchanged from dev4 (bench signature
`243f9a1c1ba5b36f`, `bench --depth 16` `a14ab62224f837e5`, ctest 11/11).

To play at the measured strength, send (the parameter file ships inside the
release archive):

```
setoption name EvalParams value params_abc.txt
setoption name TTEval value true
```

With exactly those options, this release measured against the pinned dev4
binary (`stockbear-dev4-1c5b61a7`, sha256
`1c5b61a755215134a030b9bf3b55876f7d287e1c965591ff0d22b485c0743aae`):

| experiment | build | games | clustered 95 % CI | LCB95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| exp-0024 (release artifact) | portable `-mpopcnt -mbmi2 -mlzcnt -DSB_SEE_CACHE=1 -flto=4` | 6600 @ 40+4 ms | **+64.7 [+57.5, +72.0]** | **+57.5 > +50 ✓** |
| exp-0023 (native runner build, not shipped) | same + `-march=native` | 6600 @ 40+4 ms | +66.4 [+59.3, +73.6] | +59.3 > +50 ✓ |

Both were pre-registered (committed before the runs), run on fresh untouched
opening suites (exp0002 / exp0001, 2200 paired openings each, excluding all
prior suites), 12 shards x 550 games with distinct seeds, paired openings with
reversed colours, hash 16 MB, threads 1, on isolated GitHub-hosted runners,
with a 1100-game candidate-vs-candidate null (exp-0024: +1.3 [−8.0, +10.6],
exp-0023: −1.3 [−11.7, +9.2] — both consistent with zero). SPRT(0,5) accepted
H1 in both (LLR 28.96 / 30.74). Zero forfeits in exp-0023; exp-0024 had one
time forfeit BY THE BASELINE (counted as its loss per the pre-declared
symmetric policy). All 6600 games are accounted for in both experiments
(6585 adjudicated + 15 unadjudicated = 6600 for exp-0024; 6581 + 19 = 6600 for
exp-0023 — the pooled report's "18" was pair-level, one pair had both games
capped). Independent audits (`scripts/audit_exp0023.py`) recomputed both
experiments from the raw records without sharing code with the original
pooling and reproduced the pooled estimates to full double precision.

**The +64.7 Elo claim attaches to the shipped Linux x64 artifact + the two
options above.** It is NOT claimed for the Windows artifact (separate MSVC
build, same source and options, bench-identical search but not separately
strength-gated), and not for any other build flags.

## What is new in the source

- exp-0019: integer UCI options `AspirationWindow`, `FutilityMargin`,
  `RevFutilityMargin`, `DeltaMargin` (defaults are the dev4 values; changing
  them clears the TT). Screens showed no reliable gain over defaults, so the
  champion config uses defaults for these.
- exp-0022: four new evaluation features (`RookOn7th`, `KnightOutpost`,
  `BackwardPawn`, `PawnChain`) appended with shipped value 0 — the default
  build stays bit-identical (bench-pinned); the tuned `params_abc.txt` gives
  them non-zero values.
- Compile-time ablations (`STOCKBEAR_SAFE_MOBILITY`, `SB_INCREMENTAL_EVAL`,
  `SB_QEVAL_LITE`, `SB_SEE_CACHE`) are all OFF by default; the release build
  enables only `SB_SEE_CACHE=1` (a semantics-preserving reuse of the SEE
  result, bench-pinned) plus the x86-64-v3 ISA flags.
- Linux TT allocation asks for transparent huge pages (`madvise` hint only;
  contents and behaviour unchanged).
- `FullSoftBudget` UCI switch (default off) for the dev5 time-management
  experiment; off in the champion config.
- Tests: 11/11 ctest entries (unit, perft, UCI, dead positions, nnue,
  tournament harness, statistics, nnue_features differential).

## Verification

- CI on the exact release commit: Linux Debug/Release, Windows Debug/Release,
  Linux Clang Release, ASan+UBSan, ThreadSanitizer, minimum CMake 3.16,
  independent reference/statistics/dead-positions jobs — all green (see the
  CI run linked below; this document does not substitute for it).
- Clean local Release build of the release commit: ctest **11/11**, perft(6)
  119,060,324, `bench` signature `243f9a1c1ba5b36f`, `bench --depth 16`
  `a14ab62224f837e5`, UCI smoke (`uci`/`isready`/`go depth`/`bestmove`).
- The packaged Linux binary is additionally exercised by the post-publish
  verification job (uci handshake, version string, both bench signatures).

## Evidence

- [exp-0023 pre-registration](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev5/docs/EXP0023_PREREG.md) and
  [confirmation](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev5/docs/EXP0023_CONFIRMATION.md) — native-build gate +66.4
  [+59.3, +73.6].
- [exp-0024 pre-registration](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev5/docs/EXP0024_PREREG.md) and
  [confirmation](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev5/docs/EXP0024_CONFIRMATION.md) — **release-artifact gate
  +64.7 [+57.5, +72.0]**.
- [independent audit report](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev5/docs/EXP0023_AUDIT.md) and the machine-readable
  audits `benchmarks/exp-runs/exp0023-audit.json` / `exp0024-audit.json`
  (recomputed from raw records by `scripts/audit_exp0023.py`).
- Raw match records (PGN + JSONL + CSV + per-shard manifests):
  [exp-0023 shards](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev5/benchmarks/exp-runs/exp0023-shard01/),
  [exp-0023 null](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev5/benchmarks/exp-runs/exp0023-null/),
  [exp-0024 shards](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev5/benchmarks/exp-runs/exp0024-shard01/),
  [exp-0024 null](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev5/benchmarks/exp-runs/exp0024-null/); pooled estimates
  `exp0023-pooled.json` / `exp0024-pooled.json`.
- [append-only failure ledger](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev5/benchmarks/FAILURE_LEDGER.md) — every failed
  gate and screen (dev5 +15.9, dev6 +47.5, dev7 +39.9, NNUE −652..−760,
  option-off ablations, ...) is preserved with its raw records.
- [dev4 evidence report](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev5/benchmarks/results/0.1.0-dev4/REPORT.md) and
  [research docs](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev5/docs/).

## Compatibility

- Linux x64 artifact: requires **x86-64-v3** (POPCNT, BMI2, LZCNT — Intel
  Haswell 2013+ / AMD Excavator 2015+). It is NOT built with
  `-march=native` and runs on any such CPU; the exp-0024 +64.7 Elo was
  measured on exactly this build.
- Windows x64 artifact: MSVC build with `/arch:AVX2` (AVX2 required) and the
  same `SB_SEE_CACHE=1` define; same source and options, bench-identical
  search, but not separately strength-gated.
- Standard UCI: `uci`, `isready`, `ucinewgame`, `position`, `go`
  (depth/nodes/movetime/clocks/increments/movestogo/infinite/searchmoves),
  `stop`, `quit`, `debug`, `info` lines. Options: `Hash`, `MultiPV`,
  `EvalParams`, `NNUE`, `NnueFile`, the boolean search switches, the four
  integer margin options, `FullSoftBudget`. No `Threads` option: the search
  is single-threaded. Ponder, Chess960, opening book and tablebases are not
  implemented. The NNUE network is not embedded; `NNUE true` reports that it
  cannot be honoured (the measured network loses ~700 Elo to the classical
  evaluation and is not shipped as default — see the dev4 notes).

## Known limitations / deferred research

- exp-0020 (fresh-corpus retune, screen +80.2 [+55.4, +105.9] on the native
  build) is **unconfirmed future research**, not part of this release's
  claims.
- The strength numbers are at 40+4 ms per move on server CPUs; absolute Elo
  depends on hardware and time control.
- All experiments, including failures, are preserved under
  `benchmarks/exp-runs/` with their pre-registrations.


## Verified release provenance

- Commit: `c94571313a1667048468cf6d4e070400dc5ab228`
- Exact-commit CI: https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/actions/runs/41624155883
- Release binary build: https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/actions/runs/41625330533

name: StockBear v0.1.0-dev4
body:
# StockBear v0.1.0-dev4 — development prerelease

StockBear is an independent C++17 UCI chess engine. Its board, legal move
generation, state management, alpha-beta search, evaluation, dead-position
analysis and UCI controller are implemented in this repository; it neither
embeds nor calls another engine to select moves. This is an early development
release, not a stable or leading-strength engine.

## What this release is, and what it is not

dev4 builds a complete neural evaluation — features, incrementally updated
accumulator, quantised network format, scalar and AVX2 kernels, self-play data
generator, trainer, quantiser and an independent verifier — and then measures it.
At 2,500 nodes per move the trained network **loses 708 Elo** (95 % CI
[−1011, −405], 60 games) to the classical evaluation of the same binary, so it is
**not** embedded and **not** the default. The five search refinements added in the
same release were each measured against the same binary with only that option
flipped: all are neutral or negative at a fixed node budget and at a fixed time
control, so all of them stay off.

**The default configuration plays exactly as dev3 does.** The depth-6 and
depth-7 benchmark signatures are unchanged (`e06c4352681ae8eb`,
`5bceff035f2a4ae4`), and a paired match against the released dev3 binary at a
fixed node budget reproduced the same-binary null control game for game. This
release therefore claims **no strength gain**; it claims verified infrastructure
and honest negative results.

## What is new

- **Neural evaluation infrastructure**, written for this project: 768 piece-square
  features per perspective, `768 → 128 → 32 → 1` with clipped ReLUs, an
  accumulator maintained incrementally through `make_move`/`unmake_move` and
  checked against a from-scratch rebuild by `verify_state()`, a versioned
  little-endian file format with full validation, and two kernels (portable scalar
  and AVX2 behind a runtime CPUID check) that are tested for bit-identical output.
- **UCI options `NNUE` (check, default false) and `NnueFile` (string).** The
  release binary embeds no network; `NNUE true` reports why it cannot be honoured
  instead of pretending. Loading a network from a file works and is covered by
  tests. The measured network is committed under `benchmarks/training/` so the
  experiment can be reproduced, with a prominent warning that it is much weaker
  than the classical evaluation.
- **Training pipeline.** `stockbear selfplay` (seeded, reproducible),
  `scripts/nnue_features.py`, `train_nnue.py` (game-level split, best-validation
  checkpoint, corpus hashes stored in the checkpoint), `convert_nnue.py`
  (percentile calibration, rounded shifts), `verify_nnue.py` (an independent
  integer re-implementation; 0 differences on 2,000 positions) and
  `embed_nnue.py`.
- **Five switchable search refinements** — `ModernLMR`, `MoveCountPruning`,
  `IIR`, `Improving`, `TTEval` — all off by default, all measured. `razoring` is
  documented as not implemented and is not advertised.
- **A match harness that can resolve small effects.** Fixed-node play is
  deterministic, so colour-reversed pairs scored identically and the pentanomial
  had zero variance: a match could not tell a +100 Elo change from a −100 Elo one.
  `scripts/tournament.py` gained a seeded per-move node jitter, and the repository
  gained a 240-opening random suite (`benchmarks/positions/openings_dev4.txt`,
  generated by `scripts/make_openings.py`) plus `scripts/experiment_table.py` to
  rebuild the results table from the raw records.

## Verification

- CTest: **11/11** entries pass in a Release build (4.8 s), including the new
  `nnue` entry (7 tests) and the new `nnue_features` differential entry.
- `unit` group: **39** tests. (The dev3 notes said 37; the source at that tag has
  39, and the miscount is corrected here rather than carried forward.)
- Bench signatures: defaults unchanged from dev3; each dev4 switch alone changes
  the signature except `TTEval`, which is a verified no-op on this search.
- Tactics suite: 25/25 at 60,000 nodes. Endgame suite: 24/24 at 400,000 nodes,
  16/24 at 20,000 nodes — both measured on this binary, not inherited from dev3.
- CI: Linux Debug/Release, ASan+UBSan, ThreadSanitizer, Clang, minimum CMake 3.16
  and Windows Debug/Release jobs run for the release commit. Check the CI run for
  the exact commit — this document does not substitute for it. The Windows binary
  is built and tested by CI; it was not executed by hand on a Windows machine.

## Evidence

- [dev4 evidence report](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev4/benchmarks/results/0.1.0-dev4/REPORT.md) — 20 sections,
  every number traceable to a committed raw record.
- [research](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev4/docs/DEV4_RESEARCH.md), [architecture](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev4/docs/DEV4_ARCHITECTURE.md),
  [training](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev4/docs/DEV4_TRAINING.md), [benchmarks](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev4/docs/DEV4_BENCHMARKS.md),
  [limitations](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev4/docs/DEV4_LIMITATIONS.md).
- Raw match records, PGN, bench CSV and suite output:
  [benchmarks/results/0.1.0-dev4/](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev4/benchmarks/results/0.1.0-dev4/).

## Compatibility

Standard UCI: `uci`, `isready`, `ucinewgame`, `position`, `go`
(depth/nodes/movetime/clocks/increments/movestogo/infinite/searchmoves), `stop`,
`quit`, `debug`, and `info` lines with depth, seldepth, multipv, score, nodes, nps,
hashfull, time and pv. Options: `Hash`, `MultiPV`, `EvalParams`, `NNUE`,
`NnueFile` and the boolean search switches. No `Threads` option: the search is
single-threaded and advertising it would be a claim the binary cannot honour.
Ponder, Chess960, an opening book and tablebases are not implemented.

No command or option was removed or changed in meaning in this release.


## Verified release provenance

- Commit: `9b5778c97ba3d3141ea61fbf3398b7fc231bbf64`
- Exact-commit CI: https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/actions/runs/41392388489
- Release binary build: https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/actions/runs/41393160832

## Post-publication check of the downloadable assets

The archives were downloaded again from this release inside Actions and checked
(run [41393380621](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/actions/runs/41393380621)):
`sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt` passes for both archives, the archives contain
`stockbear` / `stockbear.exe` + `README.md` + `LICENSE`, the packaged Linux binary
answers `uci` with `id name StockBear 0.1.0-dev4` and reports `network=none`, and
its bench signatures are `e06c4352681ae8eb` (depth 6) and `5bceff035f2a4ae4`
(depth 7) — the dev3 signatures, as intended.

Digests, the exact commands and what was **not** verified (the Windows archive is
built and tested by CI but was not run by hand; the third-party review bot could
not run) are in
[RELEASE_ASSETS.md](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/main/benchmarks/results/0.1.0-dev4/RELEASE_ASSETS.md).

name: StockBear v0.1.0-dev3
body:
# StockBear v0.1.0-dev3 — development prerelease

StockBear is an independent C++17 UCI chess engine. Its board, legal move
generation, state management, alpha-beta search, evaluation, dead-position
analysis and UCI controller are implemented in this repository; it neither
embeds nor calls another engine to select moves. This is an early development
release, not a stable or leading-strength engine.

## What is new in dev3

- **Real `MultiPV`.** `MultiPV 1–8` reports that many distinct legal root moves
  as ranked `multipv` lines, each with its own score, principal variation, node
  count and a `bestmove` that equals line 1. Fewer legal moves than requested is
  handled by reporting fewer lines. Previously the option did not exist.
- **Real `go searchmoves`.** The list is parsed, validated against the legal root
  moves, and enforced under every kind of limit. Illegal entries are reported and
  dropped; a list with nothing legal in it is reported and ignored instead of
  answered with a dummy move; a list followed by another keyword does not swallow
  it. MultiPV and searchmoves are covered by black-box CTest entries over depth,
  nodes, movetime and clock limits.
- **The evaluation is data, not constants.** Every weight is a named parameter in
  a documented table with ranges and a provenance comment, dumpable and loadable
  (`stockbear bench --params FILE`, UCI `EvalParams`), with the dev2 values kept
  as `benchmarks/params/dev2-baseline.txt` so the previous behaviour is
  identifiable and reproducible byte for byte.
- **An offline tuning pipeline.** `scripts/tune_eval.py` fits the parameter table
  to a generated self-play corpus with separate training/holdout splits, recorded
  seeds, checksums and command lines. It is reproducible and it is honest: the
  three candidates it produced were matched against the shipped evaluation and
  **none of them improved on it** (−132.5 Elo, confirmed worse by both reported
  intervals; 0.0 and −9.2 Elo, indistinguishable from the shipped set; 582–600
  decided games each), and a fourth, more conservative fit moves
  seven positional terms by one or two points without a match to justify them.
  The shipped release therefore keeps the dev2 coefficients. Record and
  reproduction commands: [docs/TUNING.md](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev3/docs/TUNING.md).
- **Five new search-ordering features, implemented, tested and left off.**
  Counter-move history, continuation history, capture history, history maluses and
  a history-aware LMR adjustment each have an independent UCI switch and a
  documented rationale. Two matches measured them: all five on scored +1.3 Elo
  [−17.9, +20.5] against the dev2 binary, and the history-malus + history-LMR
  subset scored −16.2 Elo [−33.0, +0.5] against the same binary with them off.
  They are off by default, and with them off the rewrite reproduces dev2's
  benchmark signatures exactly (`e06c4352681ae8eb` at depth 6,
  `5bceff035f2a4ae4` at depth 7).
- **Tactics and endgame suites with an independent oracle.**
  `benchmarks/tactics/mate_suite.epd` (25 mate positions from StockBear self-play
  games, each re-proved by a python-chess oracle that lists *all* moves forcing
  mate inside the stated number of plies) and
  `benchmarks/tactics/endgame_suite.epd` (24 three-man endgames). Fixed-node,
  reproducible runs with raw output retained: **25/25** mates solved at 60 k
  nodes, **24/24** endgames converted at 400 k nodes.
- **A search audit with fixes.** The mate-score, transposition-table, repetition
  and fifty-move, null-move-zugzwang, interruption and PV-construction paths were
  re-derived and covered by new unit tests, including MultiPV ordering, MultiPV
  versus single-PV agreement, searchmoves restriction, and immediate termination in
  terminal positions. The `counterMoves` comment inconsistency was resolved by
  documenting what the code actually does rather than by changing behaviour.
- **Determinism and option honesty.** The advertised default of every check option
  is now read from the live configuration instead of being hard-coded, so a
  default can never drift from what the search uses.

## Strength statement for dev3

**dev3 does not claim to be stronger than dev2, and is not.** Its search and
evaluation are the dev2 ones with the new features switched off; a 200-game
paired regression match against a rebuilt `v0.1.0-dev2` binary scored 0.5000
(70 =60 −70), with 70 pairs split one win each way and 30 pairs drawn twice, so
every one of the 100 pairs scored 1.0. dev2's own
strength result stands unchanged: **+235.4 Elo over dev1** (400 paired games,
opening-clustered 95 % interval +193.4 to +284.5) and **0.5/20 against
Stockfish 11**. No match against Stockfish 19 was possible in the release
environment (its NNUE network assets are unreachable there and every archived
network available was architecture-incompatible); the attempts are recorded in
the evidence report. No superiority or parity claim is made against any engine.

## Evidence

[benchmarks/results/0.1.0-dev3/REPORT.md](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev3/benchmarks/results/0.1.0-dev3/REPORT.md)
— build identity, benchmark signatures and per-set nodes, both search-feature
matches, the regression match, the three evaluation matches, the suite runs with
raw engine output, and the blocked Stockfish 19 attempts with their error text.
[benchmarks/results/0.1.0-dev3/tuning/](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev3/benchmarks/results/0.1.0-dev3/tuning/) —
the generated dataset manifest, the three parameter variants and their matches.

Verification: CTest entries `unit` (37 tests), `position_extra`, `regression`,
`perft_quick`, `perft_full`, `stress`, `deadpos`, `uci_integration` and
`uci_fuzz`; Linux GCC Debug/Release, ASan+UBSan and ThreadSanitizer runs; Clang
Release and minimum-CMake-3.16 CI jobs; Windows Debug/Release CI. Check the CI
runs for the exact release commit — this document does not substitute for them.

## Compatibility

Standard UCI: `uci`, `isready`, `ucinewgame`, `position`, `go`
(depth/nodes/movetime/clocks/increments/movestogo/infinite/searchmoves), `stop`,
`quit`, `debug`, and `info` lines with depth, seldepth, multipv, score, nodes, nps,
hashfull, time and pv. Options: `Hash` (1–512 MiB), `MultiPV` (1–8),
`EvalParams` (a parameter file), plus the boolean search-feature switches. The
five dev3 ordering switches default to off. There is no `Threads` option: the
search is single-threaded and advertising a thread option that does nothing would
be misleading. A terminal position returns `bestmove 0000`.

## Platforms and limitations

Linux x64 and Windows x64 are the release targets; CI builds and tests Linux and
Windows Debug/Release and produces the Release archives. No AVX2/AVX-512, GPU or
external engine is required at run time, and builds are portable (no
`-march=native`).

Known limitations: the search has no fifty-move or progress term, so a won
endgame can in principle still be shuffled into a claimable repetition (no
position in the committed suite does at 400 k nodes, but the mechanism is
unchanged); the evaluation tuning did not improve play; all matches are
node-limited and therefore measure strength per node rather than per second;
there is no Stockfish 19 measurement.

The dead-position analysis is exact but exponential in the worst case; positions
whose reachable component exceeds the configured budget return `unknown` rather
than a guess. FEN cannot encode earlier repetition history, so a GUI/referee must
still adjudicate claims. No Chess960, pondering, tablebases, opening book, neural
evaluation or training system is provided.

Apache-2.0. Optional validation and opponent software is recorded in
[THIRD_PARTY.md](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev3/THIRD_PARTY.md).

---

# Earlier release: StockBear v0.1.0-dev2 — development prerelease

The notes for the previous prerelease are kept verbatim below for provenance.

## What is new in dev2

- **A general FIDE Article 5.2.2 dead-position decision procedure.** The
  detector proves `Alive` with a checkmate witness or `Dead` by exhaustively
  enumerating the complete reachable state component, and says `Unknown`
  otherwise. It finds dead positions that no material rule can see (14 blocked
  pawns: 768 distinct states; locked pawn chains with bishops: 152,352 distinct
  states reached by 1,268,497 move applications) and
  refuses to call provably alive positions dead (`KNN` v `K`, `KB` v `KN`,
  `KN` v `KN`). New CLI: `stockbear deadpos --fen FEN`. Details, correctness
  argument and limits: [docs/DEAD_POSITIONS.md](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev3/docs/DEAD_POSITIONS.md).
- **A substantially faster and stronger search**: aspiration windows, null-move
  pruning, late move reductions, reverse futility and futility pruning, static
  exchange evaluation, delta pruning in quiescence, mate-distance pruning, a
  better move picker and a real soft/hard time budget.
- **Measurable evidence**: the depth-6 benchmark suite went from 1,683,192 to
  108,910 nodes (622 ms → 49 ms, measured alternately in one idle session), the
  depth-7 suite from 8,276,659 to 250,053 nodes, and 400 paired games against dev1
  scored +277 =82 −41, i.e. **Elo +235.4 with a 95 % interval of +193.4 to
  +284.5** (opening-clustered over the 31 distinct openings; the plain pentanomial
  interval over the 200 opening pairs, which treats them as independent, is the
  narrower +202.8 to +272.2).
- **Honest tournament statistics**: Wilson intervals, a pentanomial model over
  opening pairs, an approximate SPRT, seeded opening shuffling, 31 verified
  openings, and a harness that records time forfeits and capped games instead of
  inventing draws.
- **Safer draw and protocol behaviour**: dead-position adjudication is separate
  from the search's cheap material heuristic, the null-move counter drift is
  fixed, and unknown `go` tokens are ignored as UCI requires instead of
  refusing the search.
- **Ablation switches**: `bench --param feature=0|1` and the matching UCI check
  options make every search feature measurable by nodes *and* by match.

## Evidence

Raw data, commands and interpretation:
[benchmarks/results/0.1.0-dev2/REPORT.md](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev3/benchmarks/results/0.1.0-dev2/REPORT.md)

# StockBear v0.1.0-dev2 — development prerelease

analysis and UCI controller are implemented in this repository; it neither
embeds nor calls another engine to select moves. This is an early development
release, not a stable or leading-strength engine.

## What is new in dev2

- **A general FIDE Article 5.2.2 dead-position decision procedure.** The
  detector proves `Alive` with a checkmate witness or `Dead` by exhaustively
  enumerating the complete reachable state component, and says `Unknown`
  otherwise. It finds dead positions that no material rule can see (14 blocked
  pawns: 768 distinct states; locked pawn chains with bishops: 152,352 distinct
  states reached by 1,268,497 move applications) and
  refuses to call provably alive positions dead (`KNN` v `K`, `KB` v `KN`,
  `KN` v `KN`). New CLI: `stockbear deadpos --fen FEN`. Details, correctness
  argument and limits: [docs/DEAD_POSITIONS.md](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev2/docs/DEAD_POSITIONS.md).
- **A substantially faster and stronger search**: aspiration windows, null-move
  pruning, late move reductions, reverse futility and futility pruning, static
  exchange evaluation, delta pruning in quiescence, mate-distance pruning, a
  better move picker and a real soft/hard time budget.
- **Measurable evidence**: the depth-6 benchmark suite went from 1,683,192 to
  108,910 nodes (622 ms → 49 ms, measured alternately in one idle session), the
  depth-7 suite from 8,276,659 to 250,053 nodes, and 400 paired games against dev1
  scored +277 =82 −41, i.e. **Elo +235.4 with a 95 % interval of +193.4 to
  +284.5** (opening-clustered over the 31 distinct openings; the plain pentanomial
  interval over the 200 opening pairs, which treats them as independent, is the
  narrower +202.8 to +272.2).
- **Honest tournament statistics**: Wilson intervals, a pentanomial model over
  opening pairs, an approximate SPRT, seeded opening shuffling, 31 verified
  openings, and a harness that records time forfeits and capped games instead of
  inventing draws.
- **Safer draw and protocol behaviour**: dead-position adjudication is separate
  from the search's cheap material heuristic, the null-move counter drift is
  fixed, and unknown `go` tokens are ignored as UCI requires instead of
  refusing the search.
- **Ablation switches**: `bench --param feature=0|1` and the matching UCI check
  options make every search feature measurable by nodes *and* by match.

name: StockBear v0.1.0-dev1
body:
# StockBear v0.1.0-dev1 — development prerelease

StockBear is a new independent C++17 UCI engine. Its board, legal move generation, state management, alpha-beta search, evaluation and UCI controller are implemented here; it neither embeds nor calls another engine to select moves. This is an early development release, not a stable or leading-strength engine.

## Included

- Standard chess legal moves, FEN and reversible state, castling, en passant, all promotions, checks, mate/stalemate, repetition and move-count draw detection.
- Iterative deepening, negamax alpha-beta/PVS, quiescence, a bounded transposition table and Zobrist keys, capture ordering, killer/history heuristics, limited check extensions and single-threaded time/cancellation handling.
- Handcrafted tapered material/positional evaluation; **no neural network**.
- UCI `uci`, `isready`, `ucinewgame`, `position`, `go` with depth/nodes/movetime/clocks/increments/movestogo/infinite, `stop`, `quit`, `debug`, and the `Hash` option. Unsupported UCI extensions are listed in the README.
- Perft/divide, deterministic fixed-depth/node benchmark suites, an optional paired UCI match/PGN harness, and CTest plus independent validation tools.

## Evidence

Nine perft positions passed their independently regenerated expected totals, including Kiwipete depth 4 = 4,085,603. A separate seed-20261030 differential run matched python-chess on 2,000 legal positions and eight curated cases at depth two. Local Debug/Release CTest and Linux ASan+UBSan runs exercised the code; check CI for results on the exact release commit and for Windows validation.

On a two-vCPU Xeon 2.60 GHz Linux guest with GCC 12.2 `-O3`, one thread and 16 MiB requested hash, the start-position depth-5 search used 17,075 nodes and 7,764 µs (about 2.20 million nodes/s); the full raw data, hardware, flags and methodology are in [the benchmark report](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev1/benchmarks/results/0.1.0-dev1/REPORT.md). An exploratory eight-game, paired-opening match at 1.0 s + 0.02 s against external Stockfish 11 ended 0 wins, 0 draws, 8 losses. The very small sample is not a precise Elo estimate. There was no Stockfish 19 match or superiority claim.

## Platforms and limitations

Linux x64 and Windows 10 x64 are the intended targets; the CI matrix builds and tests Windows and Linux Debug/Release and makes Release artifacts available when its jobs pass. The executable uses no Python or external chess engine at runtime. It does not require AVX-512 or a GPU.

The dead-position detector recognizes common material cases, not all blocked FIDE dead positions. FEN cannot encode pre-FEN repetition history; GUIs/referees must adjudicate draw claims. Search is single-threaded and uses baseline time/evaluation heuristics; no Chess960, pondering, `searchmoves`, MultiPV, tablebases, opening book, neural network or training system is provided. Future work is described in [the roadmap](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev1/docs/ROADMAP.md).

Apache-2.0; optional validation and opponent licenses are recorded in [THIRD_PARTY.md](https://github.com/coderunknow/StockBear/blob/v0.1.0-dev1/THIRD_PARTY.md).
